title: Roanoke's Lost Colony: What Did CROATOAN Mean? | Curio Files
description:
Over 110 people were gone, yet CROATOAN on a post made Governor John White glad. In his own account, it was their agreed message for moving away, pointing to the Croatoan people's island, roughly today's Hatteras Island area.
Curio Files H02. From the farewell in 1587 to an empty fort at dawn in 1590: CRO on a tree, CROATOAN on a palisade post, no distress cross, dismantled houses and rain-damaged chests. He understood where to look. Why did he still fail to find the people?
What can later ancestral stories, drought, carved stones, a brass ring and a map patch each tell us? The island and inland archaeological searches offer clues, alongside questions about dating and trade. Between a destination and a solved case, we still need evidence identifying people and settlements as belonging to the colonists.

The main historical and archaeological sources and the images used were refreshed on 2026-10-12; the remaining research was checked on 2026-10-10. White's original return account is the sole surviving eyewitness text of that visit. Later retellings and modern research are not treated as his own observations.
Illustrations were generated with AI. The engraving, baptism scene and ruins image are later works, not records made on site in 1587. The carving's position in the 1893 ruins image also differs from the eyewitness text.

thumbnail.headline: **Not a Spell**
thumbnail.sub: He knew where, found no one.

530240f0.text: Over 100 were gone. Yet White wrote that he was glad.

c396bf52.text: You might think Croatoan was some mysterious code.

f8974907.text: It was a place name: their agreed sign for moving away.

5cae000c.text: So why couldn't he find them?

abb7999e.text: The carving told him where to look.

37eb7619.text: A destination, but no trace of the people.

ad443391.text: In July 1587, the fleet brought families here.

0378a93d.text: This arrival print appeared after contact was lost.

7d3976ee.text: Their intended home was a bay farther north.

de9770ac.text: Chesapeake Bay was the goal; this was a stopover.

e8e1f755.text: The pilot refused to go north; they had to stay at Roanoke.

609abd25.text: Not new ground: earlier English settlers had lived here.

cb08d4da.text: Melons filled the old homes. White saw deer go in to eat them.

bd947762.text: Over 110 people began repairs to make this place home.

07721bae.text: Manteo, a Croatoan, helped the English speak with his people.

f6e27da0.text: White called the islanders friends, but relations weren't always peaceful.

069ea2a2.text: An English attack on Croatoans by mistake had caused a rift.

1ff46026.text: Food was uncertain. With winter near, supplies became urgent.

86a65e1b.text: This baptism scene was imagined over 200 years later.

51dcd3dc.text: Governor White's daughter had a baby girl on August 18.

9950a707.text: His granddaughter, Virginia Dare, was the colony's new life.

55c9e647.text: Aug 22: they ask White to return home for aid

385bc548.text: The joint letter of the 25th confirms they sent him back.

be38542e.text: He left on the morning of the 27th. The baby was just 9 days old.

ea6f1c25.text: Reluctant at first, he sailed home with their plea.

1b1b3b7d.text: Before he left, they agreed: if moving, carve the new place name.

421fe082.text: There was also a plan to move about 50 miles inland.

e86ab0b4.text: If in danger, they would carve a cross above the place name.

e4b5d68e.text: He hoped to return next spring, but faced delay after delay.

5a4ea7a7.text: The Spanish Armada drew near. England had to defend itself.

deafa764.text: 1588: war and trade ships must stay by England.

590718a5.text: 1588: supply ships fought the French and returned.

384b98db.text: Only in 1590 did a privateer agree to take him there on its way.

7ca9a959.text: He'd only gone for supplies. What would he find on returning?

53923c71.text: On August 18, 1590, White returned to Roanoke.

6387c813.text: Trumpets and songs the night before drew no reply from shore.

c8106dd9.text: At dawn they landed, crossing sand to find the old homes.

6abe644b.text: First, on a tree trunk: only Croatoan's first three letters.

8697084e.text: The other: a bark-stripped post at the palisade gate.

01e14e26.text: Three letters on the tree; the full CROATOAN on the post.

527830a9.text: The post's carving was high: about 1.5 meters off the ground.

543e602a.text: The houses were dismantled, not simply empty rooms.

3ee52e06.text: Tall trunks formed a wall around the homes, like a defensive fort.

d30453cd.text: Iron bars and lead lay inside, the heavy items nearly weed-covered.

86b291b5.text: By the creek, they sought old boats and a few small cannon left there.

9e5b48ba.text: None were found. That didn't tell them who took them.

c11d2375.text: At the old trench's end were 5 chests, once hidden, then dug up.

435e5db2.text: Three were White's; what he left here was ruined.

3f471fa8.text: Book covers torn off; frames and maps ruined by rain.

a1530843.text: The armor was badly rusted. The chests couldn't say where people went.

344d40fb.text: Damaged chests don't prove the whole colony was attacked.

ecc48106.text: White blamed local enemies: his guess about the chests.

369cdc7d.text: Move: carve a place name. In distress: add a cross. That was their agreement.

d510fc74.text: The post read CROATOAN, with no distress cross.

ddac8184.text: White wrote of joy, thinking them safe on friends' island.

e3138e28.text: His reading of that message, not everyone's later fate.

4b1ee5e0.text: Only White left eyewitness writing; most later accounts retell it.

5c3267a5.text: He had a place. What step remained to find them?

f842d461.text: Croatoan named a tribe and the place where they lived.

948e50c0.text: Roughly today's Hatteras Island area, south of Roanoke.

d37cb405.text: The plan: about 50 miles inland to a better home.

9ee17073.text: Now the message pointed to the southern island, a different direction.

ced77e9e.text: Two 50-mile routes can't become one plan to move.

69efb42f.text: White saw it as friends' island and planned a coastal search.

ebd0c9ba.text: Setting off, another cable snapped and the ship lost an anchor.

8a6d5e5d.text: Of 4 anchors with cables, 1 set was left as wind and waves rose.

b9a5329e.text: Water casks stayed ashore; food aboard was running short.

7de7ba3d.text: Holding the ship grew more urgent than finding the message.

737af853.text: First, resupply south; return after winter to find them.

148173a7.text: They aimed for the Trinidad area: water and food first.

7b5dbe96.text: An August 28 storm blocked their planned route again.

9b24aa1a.text: They had to head to the Azores, then an English port.

89cdc105.text: The destination was clear, but bad weather stopped their search.

bd649f94.text: White never reached Croatoan or brought news of his family.

adeea438.text: His landing fell on his granddaughter's third birthday.

c2450101.text: Did anyone later leave clues about these 100-plus people?

72d80a5e.text: An ancestral story entered the record only over a century later.

04fe502e.text: Lawson's 1709 book recorded the islanders' ancestor story.

d1c58c2b.text: The Hatteras spoke of white forebears who read like the English.

e8d5e691.text: It wasn't a record made there in 1587.

aae17c5d.text: An ancestral story, over a century later.

a9e17aca.text: It still can't identify any one colonist.

56df705f.text: Another story said Powhatan ordered the colonists killed.

4f036f32.text: Strachey retold it; no record says he witnessed the massacre.

7068cff0.text: Virginia's tree rings hold another clue to the pressures of survival.

10df3871.text: Those 3 colonial years saw regional drought.

dd29a13e.text: Regional drought may have strained food supplies, but can't say where people went.

c3df0b73.text: By the 19th century, the Lost Colony had become a literary subject.

8b0f9364.text: Here, a big tree bears the place name.

8c0f94f7.text: This is a later imagining, from 1893.

9a193f80.text: From 1937, 40-odd carved stones emerged, claiming to tell their fate.

b2a1a98c.text: Most were later judged fake. The first remains unresolved.

03ad5279.text: Rumors can't close it. How do we assess dug-up objects?

eb0658d3.text: Objects give no names. Check material, then age and where they were found.

b9949b9c.text: A ring was dug up on Hatteras.

ba949d2f.text: Thought gold, a clue to an English family.

21a67841.text: Later analysis found brass, made of copper and zinc.

3c1a27d4.text: The material was known, but who wore the ring was still uncertain.

adae2990.text: Tests show the ring is brass

aeae2b23.text: But they can't identify its past owner.

14d603d3.text: Objects near the ring dated into the early 18th century.

ab3af46c.text: Other European finds mixed with mid-17th-century objects.

8087c100.text: So a European object can't simply be assigned to 1587.

15e3784d.text: Beyond its age, check the layer of earth where it was found.

73e32f2b.text: Are these things from the same period?

515ebefd.text: European goods could also reach Native villages through trade.

f9f6eb48.text: An object's origin doesn't identify the person who brought it here.

3bd684e6.text: Another search began with a patch hiding a symbol on White's map.

0e523c82.text: The fort-like mark beneath pointed inland, west of Roanoke.

c9ab868d.text: Inland Bertie County digs kept finding English-made objects.

dd06c68a.text: They found 2 sites with clusters of objects, one by one.

f93ec640.text: The team read these sites as signs of scattered colonial farms.

b475efb8.text: In June 2026, the team announced success.

c556a225.text: The Park Service theory page was updated a year before this claim.

a2a221f7.text: Linking find sites to a colony needs independent testing.

40e75a82.text: To link objects to colonists, rule out later arrival and trade.

4b1e4b43.text: What evidence would truly close this case?

6aaa024d.text: To close it, link the objects to where those people lived.

c33bbeea.text: If houses can be traced to them, objects gain context from daily life.

7aaa7142.text: Earlier Park Service work hadn't identified their village.

3acd91a4.text: Scattering or joining others: later theories.

6469b019.text: White saw the carving but couldn't verify where his family had gone.

2b2d8064.text: Moving, scattering, joining others: possibilities suggested by clues.

f08503c5.text: These objects alone still can't reveal each person's final fate.

9b2c16c8.text: The grandfather read their moving notice, but never got there.

bf77b9cc.text: A destination in the record; the search voyage was never finished.
